-addpreferredwirelessnetworkatindex.Name: -addpreferredwirelessnetworkatindex
-addpreferredwirelessnetworkatindex.description: Add wireless network named <network> to preferred list for <hardwareport> at <index>. Store the optional password in the keychain

-create6to4service.Name: -create6to4service
-create6to4service.description: Use this command to create a new 6 to 4 service with name <newnetworkservicename>

-createBond.Name: -createBond
-createBond.description: Create a bond with the user-defined-name name and optionally add any listed devices if they support bonding

-createVLAN.Name: -createVLAN
-createVLAN.description: Create a VLAN with the name <name> over the parent device <parentdevice> and with the tag <tag>

-createlocation.Name: -createlocation
-createlocation.description: Create a set with the user-defined-name name and optionally populate it with the default services

-createnetworkservice.Name: -createnetworkservice
-createnetworkservice.description: Create a service named <networkservice> on port <hardwareport>. The new service will be enabled by default

-createpppoeservice.Name: -createpppoeservice
-createpppoeservice.description: Create a PPPoE service on the specified device with the service name specified

-deleteBond.Name: -deleteBond
-deleteBond.description: Delete the bond with the specified device-name

-deleteVLAN.Name: -deleteVLAN
-deleteVLAN.description: Delete the VLAN with the name <name> over the parent device <parentdevice> and with the tag <tag>

-detectnewhardware.Name: -detectnewhardware
-detectnewhardware.description: Detects new network hardware and creates a default network service on the hardware

-duplicatenetworkservice.Name: -duplicatenetworkservice
-duplicatenetworkservice.description: Use this command to duplicate an existing network service <networkservice> and rename it to the specified name <newnetworkservicename>

-getMTU.Name: -getMTU
-getMTU.description: Get the MTU value for hardwareport or device specified

-getMedia.Name: -getMedia
-getMedia.description: Show both the current setting for media and the active media on hardwareport or device specified

-getadditionalroutes.Name: -getadditionalroutes
-getadditionalroutes.description: Use this command to display the list of additional IPv4 routes configured for the service

-getairportpower.Name: -getairportpower
-getairportpower.description: Displays whether Wi-Fi power is on or off

-getautoproxyurl.Name: -getautoproxyurl
-getautoproxyurl.description: Displays proxy auto-config (url, enabled) info for <networkservice>

-getcurrentlocation.Name: -getcurrentlocation
-getcurrentlocation.description: Display the name of the current set

-getinfo.Name: -getinfo
-getinfo.description: Displays the IP address, subnet mask, router, and hardware address for the <networkservice> that you specify

-getmacaddress.Name: -getmacaddress
-getmacaddress.description: Displays ethernet (or Wi-Fi) address for hardwareport or device specified

-getnetworkserviceenabled.Name: -getnetworkserviceenabled
-getnetworkserviceenabled.description: Displays whether a service is on or off (enabled or disabled)

-getsecurewebproxy.Name: -getsecurewebproxy
-getsecurewebproxy.description: Displays Secure Web proxy (server, port, enabled value) info for <networkservice>

-getsocksfirewallproxy.Name: -getsocksfirewallproxy
-getsocksfirewallproxy.description: Displays SOCKS Firewall proxy (server, port, enabled value) info for <networkservice>

-getv6additionalroutes.Name: -getv6additionalroutes
-getv6additionalroutes.description: Use this command to display the list of additional IPv6 routes configured for the service

-getwebproxy.Name: -getwebproxy
-getwebproxy.description: Displays Web proxy (server, port, enabled value) info for <networkservice>

-help.Name: -help
-help.description: Displays a list of all the commands available in the Network Setup Tool, with explanatory information

-isBondSupported.Name: -isBondSupported
-isBondSupported.description: Displays YES if the device can be added to a bond. NO if it cannot

-listVLANs.Name: -listVLANs
-listVLANs.description: List the VLANs that have been created

-listValidMTURange.Name: -listValidMTURange
-listValidMTURange.description: List the valid MTU range for hardwareport or device specified

-listValidMedia.Name: -listValidMedia
-listValidMedia.description: List valid media options for hardwareport or device name. Enumerates available subtypes and options per subtype

-listallhardwareports.Name: -listallhardwareports
-listallhardwareports.description: Displays list of hardware ports with corresponding device name and ethernet address

-listallnetworkservices.Name: -listallnetworkservices
-listallnetworkservices.description: Displays a list of all the network services on the server's hardware ports

-listdevicesthatsupportVLAN.Name: -listdevicesthatsupportVLAN
-listdevicesthatsupportVLAN.description: List the devices that support VLANs

-listnetworkserviceorder.Name: -listnetworkserviceorder
-listnetworkserviceorder.description: Displays a list of network services in the order they are contacted for a connection, along with the corresponding port and device for each

-listpppoeservices.Name: -listpppoeservices
-listpppoeservices.description: List all PPPoE services in the current set

-listpreferredwirelessnetworks.Name: -listpreferredwirelessnetworks
-listpreferredwirelessnetworks.description: List the preferred wireless networks for <hardwareport>

-ordernetworkservices.Name: -ordernetworkservices
-ordernetworkservices.description: Use this command to designate the order network services are contacted on the specified hardware port. Name the network you want contacted first, then the second, and so on. Use "listnetworkserviceorder" to view current service order. Note: use quotes around service names which contain spaces (ie. "Built-in Ethernet")

-printcommands.Name: -printcommands
-printcommands.description: Displays a list of commands with no detail

-removeallpreferredwirelessnetworks.Name: -removeallpreferredwirelessnetworks
-removeallpreferredwirelessnetworks.description: Remove all networks from the preferred wireless network list for <hardwareport>

-removenetworkservice.Name: -removenetworkservice
-removenetworkservice.description: Use this command to delete a network service <networkservice>. You cannot use this command to delete the last remaining service for a hardware port. To do so, you use the -setnetworkserviceenabled command

-removepreferredwirelessnetwork.Name: -removepreferredwirelessnetwork
-removepreferredwirelessnetwork.description: Remove <network> from the preferred wireless network list for <hardwareport>

-renamenetworkservice.Name: -renamenetworkservice
-renamenetworkservice.description: Use this command to rename the specified network service <networkservice> to <newnetworkservicename>

-set6to4automatic.Name: -set6to4automatic
-set6to4automatic.description: Use this command to set the 6 to 4 service such that it will get the relay address automatically

-set6to4manual.Name: -set6to4manual
-set6to4manual.description: Use this command to set the 6 to 4 service such that it will get the relay address manually. Specify the <relayaddress> that you would like to set

-setMTU.Name: -setMTU
-setMTU.description: Set MTU for hardwareport or device specified

-setMTUAndMediaAutomatically.Name: -setMTUAndMediaAutomatically
-setMTUAndMediaAutomatically.description: Set hardwareport or device specified back to automatically setting the MTU and Media

-setMedia.Name: -setMedia
-setMedia.description: Set media for hardwareport or device specified to subtype. Specify optional [option1] and additional options depending on subtype. Any number of valid options can be specified

-setadditionalroutes.Name: -setadditionalroutes
-setadditionalroutes.description: Use this command to set the list of IPv4 additional routes configured for the service. Each route is specified as a (destination address, subnet mask, gateway address) tuple. Specifying no tuples clears the list of routes

-setairportnetwork.Name: -setairportnetwork
-setairportnetwork.description: Set Wi-Fi Network to <network> using optional [password] if specified

-setairportpower.Name: -setairportpower
-setairportpower.description: Set Wi-Fi power to either <on> or <off>

-setautoproxyurl.Name: -setautoproxyurl
-setautoproxyurl.description: Set proxy auto-config to url for <networkservice> and enable it

-setbootp.Name: -setbootp
-setbootp.description: Use this command to set the TCP/IP configuration for the specified <networkservice> to use BOOTP

-setcomputername.Name: -setcomputername
-setcomputername.description: Sets computer name to <computername>. This name is used by AFP

-setdhcp.Name: -setdhcp
-setdhcp.description: Use this command to set the TCP/IP configuration for the specified <networkservice> to use DHCP. The client ID is optional. Specify "Empty" for [clientid] to clear the DHCP client id

-setdnsservers.Name: -setdnsservers
-setdnsservers.description: Use this command to specify the IP addresses of servers you want the specified <networkservice> to use to resolve domain names. You can list any number of servers (replace dns1, dns2, and so on with the IP addresses of domain name servers). If you want to clear all DNS entries for the specified network service, type "empty" in place of the DNS server names

-setmanual.Name: -setmanual
-setmanual.description: Set the TCP/IP configuration for <networkservice> to manual with IP address set to <ip>, Subnet Mask set to <subnet>, and Router address set to <router>

-setmanualwithdhcprouter.Name: -setmanualwithdhcprouter
-setmanualwithdhcprouter.description: Use this command to specify a manual IP address to use for DHCP for the specified <networkservice>

-setnetworkserviceenabled.Name: -setnetworkserviceenabled
-setnetworkserviceenabled.description: Use this command to turn the specified network service on or off (enable or disable)

-setpppoeaccountname.Name: -setpppoeaccountname
-setpppoeaccountname.description: Set the account name for the service

-setpppoepassword.Name: -setpppoepassword
-setpppoepassword.description: Set the password for the service

-setproxyautodiscovery.Name: -setproxyautodiscovery
-setproxyautodiscovery.description: Set Proxy Auto Discover for <networkservice> to either <on> or <off>

-setproxybypassdomains.Name: -setproxybypassdomains
-setproxybypassdomains.description: Set the Bypass Domain Name Servers for <networkservice> to <domain1> [domain2] [...]. Any number of Domain Name servers can be specified. Specify "Empty" for <domain1> to clear all Domain Name entries

-setsearchdomains.Name: -setsearchdomains
-setsearchdomains.description: Use this command to designate the search domain for the specified <networkservice>. You can list any number of search domains (replace domain1, domain2, and so on with the name of a local domain). If you want to clear all search domain entries for the specified network service, type “empty” in place of the domain name

-setsecurewebproxy.Name: -setsecurewebproxy
-setsecurewebproxy.description: Set Secure Web proxy for <networkservice> with <domain> and <port number>. Turns proxy on. Optionally, specify <on> or <off> for <authenticated> to enable and disable authenticated proxy support. Specify <username> and <password> if you turn authenticated proxy support on

-setsecurewebproxystate.Name: -setsecurewebproxystate
-setsecurewebproxystate.description: Set Secure Web proxy on <networkservice> to either <on> or <off>

-setsocksfirewallproxy.Name: -setsocksfirewallproxy
-setsocksfirewallproxy.description: Set SOCKS Firewall proxy for <networkservice> with <domain> and <port number>. Turns proxy on.  Optionally, specify <on> or <off> for <authenticated> to enable and disable authenticated proxy support. Specify <username> and <password> if you turn authenticated proxy support on

-setsocksfirewallproxystate.Name: -setsocksfirewallproxystate
-setsocksfirewallproxystate.description: Set SOCKS Firewall proxy to  either <on> or <off>

-setv4off.Name: -setv4off
-setv4off.description: Use this command to turn IPv4 off on the specified <networkservice>

-setv6additionalroutes.Name: -setv6additionalroutes
-setv6additionalroutes.description: Use this command to set the list of additional routes configured for the service. Each route is specified as a (destination address, prefix length, gateway address) tuple. Specifying no tuples clears the list of routes

-setv6automatic.Name: -setv6automatic
-setv6automatic.description: Use this command to set IPv6 to get its addresses automatically for <networkservice>

-setv6linklocal.Name: -setv6linklocal
-setv6linklocal.description: Use this command to set IPv6 to only use link local for <networkservice>

-setv6manual.Name: -setv6manual
-setv6manual.description: Use this command to set IPv6 to get its addresses manually for <networkservice>. Specify the ip address, the prefix length and the router

-setv6off.Name: -setv6off
-setv6off.description: Use this command to turn IPv6 off on the specified <networkservice>

-setwebproxy.Name: -setwebproxy
-setwebproxy.description: Set Web proxy for <networkservice> with <domain> and <port number>. Turns proxy on. Optionally, specify <on> or <off> for <authenticated> to enable and disable authenticated proxy support. Specify <username> and <password> if you turn authenticated proxy support on

-setwebproxystate.Name: -setwebproxystate
-setwebproxystate.description: Set Web proxy on <networkservice> to either <on> or <off>

-showBondStatus.Name: -showBondStatus
-showBondStatus.description: Display the status of the specified bond

-showpppoestatus.Name: -showpppoestatus
-showpppoestatus.description: Display the status of the PPPoE service with the specified name

-switchtolocation.Name: -switchtolocation
-switchtolocation.description: Make the specified set the current set
